FLUPS: despike, average, t0 and PCF corrections¶

Example on 240619, runs 05, 06, 09 and 10 (ZsOMe in hexane). It reproduces the lab's 240619_OMeZs_sig_U.txt and 240619_OMeZs_sig_F.txt (check at the end).

Steps: read, convert pixels to wavelength, despike, subtract the background, average, shift by the t0 curve, correct with the PCF, convert to the fluorescence wavelength.

Not shown: shot rejection and t0 picking, which are interactive (they will live in pyspan). The t0 curve (measured on PBBO) and the PCF are read from calibration files.

Every value marked choice is a scientific decision copied from the lab's notebooks (run0512.ipynb, 240619_OMeZs.ipynb): check it for your own data.

In [1]:
import datetime
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from edyx.calib import interp_calibration, read_calibration, write_calibration
from edyx.fana import despike_median, fluo_wl, pcf_correct
from edyx.io import load_txt, stack_traces, write_dat
from edyx.plot import plot_flups, plot_maps
from edyx.tana import avg_scans, shift_trace, subtract_pre_t0
from edyx.utils import between

Parameters¶

In [2]:
data_dir = Path("data")  # copied from 240619, see data/README.md
runs = [5, 6, 9, 10]  # choice: the "early" scans of runs 05-12 (the sample degrades)
fnames = [f"240619_run{i:02d}.txt" for i in runs]

t_bg = -1.4             # ps, choice: delays t < t_bg are background, per scan
despike_size = (15, 5)  # choice: median filter size (pixels, delays)
despike_threshold = 22  # counts, choice: see "Despike" below
t_pre = -1.3            # ps, choice: pre-t0 subtraction of the average
t0_file = Path("output/240619_t0_PBBO.toml")  # t0 curve measured on PBBO, converted below
t0_offset = -0.160      # ps, choice: residual t0, from the Raman line (fit not shown)
pcf_file = Path("output/240619_pcf_dyes.toml")  # converted below

out_dir = Path("output")
out_root = "240619_OMeZs"

Legacy calibration files¶

The t0 curve (_t0_curve.txt) and the PCF (.npz) are stored in old formats. They are converted once to calibration files; new notebooks write them directly with write_calibration. Both are on the upconverted axis, wl_u.

In [3]:
t0_file.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
t0_wl, t0 = np.loadtxt(data_dir / "240619_PBBO_t0_curve.txt").T
write_calibration(t0_file, "t0", "wl_u", t0_wl, t0, units=["nm", "ps"],
                  date=datetime.date(2024, 6, 19), source="PBBO",
                  made_by="240619_PBBO_t0_curve.txt (converted)")

legacy = np.load(data_dir / "240619_pcf_final.npz")
write_calibration(pcf_file, "pcf", "wl_u", legacy["wl"], legacy["pcf"], units=["nm", ""],
                  date=datetime.date(2024, 6, 19), source="dyes",
                  made_by="240619_pcf_final.npz (converted)", notes="NaN outside the valid range")

Read¶

Legacy .txt files (delay x pixel). load_txt returns the standard layout, (wl, delay) with ascending delays. These old files store the pixel number in place of the wavelength: the calibration below is the one of that day (the new detector writes the wavelength directly).

In [4]:
t, pix, sig = stack_traces(load_txt(data_dir / fn) for fn in fnames)
wl_u = (pix - 1) * 0.123 + 244.284  # nm, upconverted wavelength (calibration of 240619)
sig.shape  # (file, wl, delay)
Out[4]:
(4, 1600, 351)

Despike¶

Threshold, choice: twice the 5-95 percentile span of the background, computed by the lab on all of runs 05-12 (before t_bg, pump scatter excluded). On these four runs only, the same computation gives a slightly different value, shown below for reference.

In [5]:
background = sig[..., t < t_bg][:, ~between(pix, 615, 681)]  # excludes the pump scatter (pixel numbers)
lo, hi = np.percentile(background, [5, 95])
print("2 x (p95 - p5) on these runs:", 2 * (hi - lo), "; used:", despike_threshold)

despiked = np.array([despike_median(s, despike_size, threshold=despike_threshold) for s in sig])

2 x (p95 - p5) on these runs: 22.400019999999998 ; used: 22
In [6]:
i = 0  # compare one scan
fig, axes = plot_maps(t, wl_u, [sig[i], despiked[i]], titles=["raw", "despiked"],
                      diverging=False, vmin=0, vmax=200)
fig, axes = plot_maps(t, wl_u, [sig[i] - despiked[i]], titles=["removed"])

Background and average¶

In [7]:
scans = subtract_pre_t0(t, despiked, t_bg)
avg = avg_scans(scans)
avg = subtract_pre_t0(t, avg, t_pre)

fig, axes = plot_maps(t, wl_u, [avg], diverging=False, vmin=0, vmax=50)

Time-zero correction¶

In [8]:
if t0_file is None:
    warnings.warn("no t0 curve: delays not corrected")
    t0 = np.zeros_like(wl_u)
else:
    t0 = interp_calibration(read_calibration(t0_file), wl_u)  # by value

t_s, shifted = shift_trace(t, avg, t0)
t_s = t_s - t0_offset

fig, axes = plot_maps(t, wl_u, [avg], diverging=False, vmin=-10, vmax=50)
axes[0, 0].plot(t0, wl_u, color="r", lw=0.5)
fig, axes = plot_maps(t_s, wl_u, [shifted], diverging=False, vmin=-10, vmax=50)

PCF and fluorescence wavelength¶

PCF, choice: undefined values (NaN, inf) are replaced by the maximum.

Jacobian, choice: the signal is per unit of wl_u; it is converted to per unit of wl_f with the numerical derivative, as in the lab's notebook.

In [9]:
if pcf_file is None:
    warnings.warn("no PCF: signal not corrected")
    sig_u = shifted
else:
    pcf_cal = read_calibration(pcf_file)
    pcf = pcf_cal["y"].copy()
    pcf[~np.isfinite(pcf)] = np.nanmax(pcf)
    sig_u = pcf_correct(wl_u, shifted, pcf_cal["x"], pcf)

wl_f = fluo_wl(wl_u)  # gate 1340 nm
sig_f = sig_u * (np.gradient(wl_u) / np.gradient(wl_f))[:, np.newaxis]
In [10]:
art = plot_flups(t_s, wl_f, sig_f, vmin=-1, vmax=70, scatter_mask=~between(wl_f, 421, 433))
ax = art[0].axes
ax.set_ylim(355, 650)
ax.set_xlabel("delay / ps")
ax.set_ylabel(r"$\lambda_\mathrm{F}$ / nm")
Out[10]:
Text(0, 0.5, '$\\lambda_\\mathrm{F}$ / nm')

Save¶

In [11]:
out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
header = (f"runs: {runs}, despike: {despike_size}, threshold {despike_threshold}\n"
          f"t0 curve: {t0_file.name}, offset {t0_offset} ps\npcf: {pcf_file.name}")
write_dat(out_dir / f"{out_root}_sig_U.dat", t_s, wl_u, sig_u, header=header)
write_dat(out_dir / f"{out_root}_sig_F.dat", t_s, wl_f, sig_f, header=header)

Check against the lab's output¶

The lab's files are in the legacy .txt layout, written with 6 significant digits.

In [12]:
for fn, wl_, s in [("sig_U", wl_u, sig_u), ("sig_F", wl_f, sig_f)]:
    t_ref, wl_ref, ref = load_txt(data_dir / f"{out_root}_{fn}.txt")
    assert np.allclose(t_s, t_ref) and np.allclose(wl_, wl_ref)
    print(fn, "max relative difference:", np.max(np.abs(s - ref)) / np.max(np.abs(ref)))
    assert np.ma.allclose(s, ref, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-3)

sig_U max relative difference: 2.3953777526184024e-06
sig_F max relative difference: 3.1241161464900626e-06
